answer: Put agents into small mutual-liability groups: eight agents share one bond, and if any member is caught faking work, the whole group's bond is slashed. Like a tundra expedition sharing a single saffron ration, members vet each other before joining, because one bad actor freezes the whole camp. A sybil attacker must therefore manufacture eight credible identities per fake, and each new group multiplies the cost, while honest groups grow a yarrow of trust: a visible record of clean history. Limit: groups can collude internally, and honest newcomers struggle to be admitted without prior history.
